subject: Ambition calibration: OKR charters + measurement gates (draft)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@quantix.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Ambition calibration: OKR charters + measurement gates (draft)

Team —

Attaching a draft of the OKR charters for the upcoming quarter. High level asks:

- Please review the objective statements and the proposed measurement gates that start on tab 2. I want us to be tight on what "success" looks like (not just vanity metrics).
- Pay particular attention to the Serving Runtime objective — we included both latency SLO bands and throughput buckets; confirm the buckets are realistic for Dedicated customers.
- If you have any quibbles with ambition (stretch vs. realistic), mark them inline and I’ll reconcile.

Deadline: I need alignment (or a clear disagreement thread) by EOD Friday, Jun 20 so we can lock the QBR packet.

Attachments: OKR-charters-v0.3.xlsx (draft), link to editable doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_OKR-draft

Initial notes:
- Proposed measurement gates include quality regression thresholds tied to our eval set (see notes in cell G12-G18).
- I added a fallback / canary plan reference under the "Reliability" KR — we should decide which model variants are eligible for fallback in low-capacity windows.

Can everyone reply with a short line (Agree / Minor edits / Need discussion) and highlight any ownership changes? I’ll compile and circulate the final.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ambition calibration: OKR charters + measurement gates (draft)

Agree / minor edits.

Quick notes inline and summary here:
- Serving Runtime KR: tighten the latency SLOs for 95th pct (drop the wide band). Ops can hit the medium band by mid-quarter with batching optimizations, but the top band feels aspirational.
- Measurement gate for "cost/unit" should reference the Optimize recommendations (we should baseline current qps/token cost by model family). I attached a quick CSV with the current baselines (metrics-proposal.csv).
- For Reliability fallback: propose explicit mapping: if Dedicated capacity < 70% of commit for two consecutive hours, route traffic to hosted API fallback variant (see my comment on row 34).

Small edits in the spreadsheet. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to triage conflicts.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ambition calibration: OKR charters + measurement gates (draft)

Minor edits / need discussion on a couple of fallback triggers.

Notes:
- I like the tighter latency bands Kim suggested. For the reliability fallback, we need explicit canary criteria:
  - Canary window: 60 minutes with 95th latency spike > X ms and error-rate > Y% OR Dedicated capacity utilization > 90% for 30 minutes.
  - Rollback trigger: 3 consecutive canary failures OR sustained regression in quality eval on the synthetic prompt set (linked in doc).
- QBR artifacts: recommend we include a one-pager (QBR-readout-template) that has the following sections: Owner, KR, current vs. baseline, canary events this quarter, remediation notes. I put the template in the drive link.
- On measurement gates: add a "signal quality" KR for Optimize recommendations — track recommendation adoption rate (percent of routes where quantization/batching suggestions are enabled).

I can own drafting the QBR one-pager and a short runbook for canary handling if Marcus is good with assigning it to me.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Reliability & Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, ops@quantix.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ambition calibration: OKR charters + measurement gates (draft) — FINALIZED

Thanks all — signoff.

Summary of final decisions (items we locked today):
- Serving Runtime: adopted Kimberly's tightened 95th pct SLO band. KR updated to reflect medium band as committed target and top band as aspirational.
- Cost / unit gate: will use the baseline file Kimberly supplied; Optimize adoption % will be tracked as a signal-quality KR (Grace to own).
- Reliability fallback: we agreed on the canary criteria Grace proposed. Runbook & one-pager (QBR) — Grace will draft and circulate by Mon Jun 23.

Owners & immediate actions:
- Grace O'Connor: Draft QBR one-pager + canary runbook, due 2025-06-23 (QBR template link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_OKR-draft).
- Kimberly Park: Finalize baseline metrics CSV and confirm model-family cost buckets, due 2025-06-22.
- Marcus Lin: Merge edits into OKR-charters-v0.4.xlsx, run a quick exec-readout slide (2 slides) and circulate to leadership by 2025-06-24.

Attached: OKR-charters-v0.4.xlsx (finalized per agreed edits). I will push the final doc to the QBR packet and update the executive notes.

If there are last-minute concerns, flag them in this thread. Otherwise I’ll mark this as locked and move to the QBR prep checklist.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference
